description: From air to meat, From earth to space
summary:
⭐ What we developed: Dremo Mars is a 3D Mars-based survival game on Roblox for kids aged 7-12. Players act as Base Commander alongside Mission Control ASTRA, learning through active decisions rather than quizzes, where every choice visibly transforms the 3D environment.


⭐ How it addresses the challenge: Built as a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, the game places kids in realistic real-time crises across an 8-room base using clearly labelled NASA example datasets. Players manage space weather in the Command Center (NASA DONKI), detect radiation hotspots and run an “air meat” lab in the Bio-Dome (NASA RadLab, Curiosity RAD), plan safe rover routes across craters in the Rover Garage (NASA Mars Trek), and produce oxygen via water-splitting in Life Support (NASA MEDLI2, MOXIE). They also purify underground ice in the Water Plant (NASA MRO, SWIM), tune delayed radio signals in the Comms Hub (NASA DSN), intercept incoming threats in the Defense Shield (NASA NEO / Eyes on Asteroids), and execute a 4-step Go / No-Go checklist at the Launch Pad (Artemis / SLS).


⭐ Why it is important: Kids discover that Mars survival relies on teamwork, hands-on science, engineering, and resource management while having fun, making future space careers feel exciting and achievable.
details:
Overall project and how does it work?

1. Game Flow & Crisis Simulation Architecture ⭐ The Flow Mechanism: Players enter the base and are briefed by Mission Control (ASTRA). A central dashboard displays base power, oxygen, and active alerts. The game combines two core elements: 🚀 Missions: Players walk to specific rooms to complete hands-on engineering and science tasks. 🚀 Commander Mode: Each Sol (Mars day) triggers events like dust storms, solar flares, meteor strikes, or oxygen faults. Players choose a plan, and the 3D base reacts dynamically (lights dim, alarms sound, dust covers panels) with no quizzes or pop-ups—kids learn from real environmental consequences.

2. Core Modules: NASA Data Sources, Student Actions, & Educational Learnings

⭐ Mission 1: Command Center (Space Weather & Magnetic Shielding)

🚀 NASA Data Source: NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database of Notifications, Knowledge, and Information).

🚀 What Kids Do: Read real-time solar intensity and coronal mass ejection (CME) graphs from past storms to manually calibrate base magnetic shield power.

🚀 What Kids Learn: Telemetry literacy, understanding how space weather impacts electrical grids, and managing energy balance under pressure.

⭐ Mission 2: Bio-Dome (Radiation Mitigation & Space Agriculture)

🚀 NASA Data Source: NASA RadLab and Curiosity RAD (~0.67 mSv per day measurement).

🚀 What Kids Do: Scan a 3D grid map to locate radiation hotspots and protect crops, plus operate the “air meat” lab (managing H2, CO2, and O2 gas valves, fermentation tanks, dryers, and 3D food printers inspired by Solar Foods' Solein and the NASA Deep Space Food Challenge).

🚀 What Kids Learn: Spatial data analysis, biochemical problem-solving, and closed-loop space food production using minimal resources.

⭐ Mission 3: Rover Garage (Topographical Navigation & Path Planning)

🚀 NASA Data Source: NASA Mars Trek elevation maps.

🚀 What Kids Do: Use a visual block-coding interface to program path-planning algorithms around actual craters and steep Martian slopes.

🚀 What Kids Learn: Foundational computational thinking, logic sequencing, and spatial awareness of Martian geography.

⭐ Mission 4: Life Support (Atmospheric Regulation & Oxygen Systems)

🚀 NASA Data Source: NASA MEDLI2 atmospheric data and MOXIE oxygen-generation parameters.

🚀 What Kids Do: Troubleshoot and fix oxygen leaks, operate a water-splitting station, and use the suit refill dock.

🚀 What Kids Learn: Electrical wiring logic, gas pressure dynamics, and systematic hardware troubleshooting.

⭐ Mission 5: Water Plant (Subsurface Ice & Hydro-Purification)

🚀 NASA Data Source: NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) and Subsurface Water Ice Mapping (SWIM).

🚀 What Kids Do: Assemble and sequence multi-stage filtration units (sediment filters, nano-membranes, and UV filters in the correct order) to convert raw Martian ice into clean water.

🚀 What Kids Learn: In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), environmental chemistry, and closed-loop water recycling principles.

⭐ Mission 6: Comms Hub (Deep Space Telemetry & Signal Tuning)

🚀 NASA Data Source: NASA Deep Space Network (DSN) latency and signal parameters. 🚀 What Kids Do: Manipulate frequency spectra and slider puzzles to filter atmospheric static and reconnect with Earth, accounting for 3 to 22 minutes of one-way delay.

🚀 What Kids Learn: Wave physics, radio frequency modulation, and the technical communication challenges of interplanetary distance.

⭐ Mission 7: Defense Shield (Orbital Mechanics & Threat Interception)

🚀 NASA Data Source: NASA Near-Earth Object (NEO) / Eyes on Asteroids datasets.

🚀 What Kids Do: Calculate incoming meteorite size, velocity, and mass to select matching defensive laser frequencies and energy output.

🚀 What Kids Learn: Applied physics (velocity, kinetic energy), mathematical estimation, and rapid decision-making in emergencies.

⭐ Mission 8: Launch Pad (Systems Integration & Flight Readiness)

🚀 NASA Data Source: NASA Artemis Program and Space Launch System (SLS) technical protocols.

🚀 What Kids Do: Complete a 4-step "Go / No-Go" pre-launch checklist across base systems before initiating final rocket ignition.

🚀 What Kids Learn: Procedural discipline, accountability, and holistic systems thinking.

3. Survival Systems & Mechanics

⭐ Spacesuit & Environment: Features a full spacesuit model with drainable/refillable oxygen, real-time base power/oxygen statistics, dynamic day/night cycles with Phobos and Deimos, 6 camera views, and a child-friendly HUD.

⭐ Data Translation: Translates one key saved NASA value per source into interactive gameplay challenges without live-feed complexity, while server scripts drive real-time world-changing effects.

⭐ Martian Atmosphere & Sky Simulation: Features a scientifically accurate environmental and lighting system based on NASA data. During daytime, the Martian sky renders a signature butterscotch/rusty orange due to airborne iron-oxide dust, while transitioning into a striking blue sunset around the sun due to Mie scattering—immersing players in authentic planetary science.

4. Tools & Software Stack

⭐ Roblox Studio: 3D world-building, terrain, physics, and lighting.

⭐ Luau: Scripting for missions, Commander mode, HUD, and mini-games.

⭐ Claude (AI Assistant): Assisted with coding architecture and testing inside Roblox Studio.

How is the project creative?

Our project, "Dremo Mars," reimagines educational gaming by blending official NASA mission datawith immersive, consequences-driven survival mechanics inside Roblox. It stands out through several key innovations:

  1. Real Data to 3D Gameplay Translation: Instead of just referencing static reports, we translate authentic NASA datasets into real-time gameplay logic and active 3D mechanics. For instance, solar weather telemetry from NASA DONKI dictates magnetic shield power calibration in the Command Center, radiation measurements from RadLab drive habitat radiation mapping, and signal latency parameters from NASA DSN power interactive frequency-tuning mini-games in the Comms Hub. Players do not just read about space; they physically interact with and solve real scientific constraints.
  2. Immersive "Commander Mode" & Environmental Consequences: The game avoids boring pop-up quizzes. Instead, a dynamic "Commander Mode" introduces real-time crises (dust storms, solar flares, and meteor strikes). The 3D base responds instantly—lights dim, alarms sound, and panels seal shut—teaching kids through authentic environmental feedback and cause-and-effect.
  3. Innovative "Meat from Air" Bio-Dome System: In the Bio-Dome, we integrate cutting-edge sustainability concepts inspired by Solar Foods' Solein technology and the NASA Deep Space Food Challenge. Players manage atmospheric gas valves , operate fermentation tanks, and utilize 3D food printers to produce protein directly from air. This introduces young learners to closed-loop life support and futuristic space agriculture.
  4. Holistic 8-Base Closed-Loop Ecosystem: Unlike standalone minigames, Dremo Mars connects 8 specialized functional bases (Command Center, Bio-Dome, Rover Garage, Life Support, Water Plant, Comms Hub, Defense Shield, and Launch Pad). Every system is interdependent, teaching holistic systems thinking, resource management, and procedural discipline under pressure.

What benefits of this project?

  1. Translates Complex Science into Engaging Gameplay: Players learn authentic NASA and space agency data—such as solar weather telemetry, radiation measurements, and topographical maps—through interactive 3D gameplay rather than boring textbooks.
  2. Fosters Critical Thinking & Crisis Problem-Solving: Through "Commander Mode," players face real-time environmental crises (like dust storms or solar flares), requiring them to analyze situations, make quick decisions, and learn from immediate cause-and-effect consequences.
  3. Sparks Awareness of Future Food Technologies: The "Meat from Air" Bio-Dome feature introduces players to closed-loop life support and futuristic protein production inspired by the NASA Deep Space Food Challenge and Solein technology.
  4. Promotes Holistic Systems Thinking: Managing eight interconnected bases teaches players how resources, energy, power, and oxygen rely on each other in a closed-loop Martian ecosystem.
  5. Builds Engineering Mindsets & Procedural Discipline: Players gain hands-on experience with engineering workflows, telemetry tracking, path-planning logic, and pre-launch system checks, inspiring the next generation of space explorers.

What is the intended impact of the project?

  1. Inspiring the Next Generation of Space Explorers: By transforming complex NASA data and space science into an immersive Roblox gaming experience, Dremo Mars sparks children's curiosity and passion for STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) fields early on.
  2. Promoting Real-World Environmental & Resource Literacy: The project educates players on critical global and interplanetary challenges—such as space weather, radiation shielding, closed-loop water recycling, and sustainable food production (via the "Meat from Air" Bio-Dome)—fostering a deep understanding of sustainability both on Mars and Earth.
  3. Cultivating Critical Thinking and Resilient Problem-Solving: Through non-linear "Commander Mode" crises and hands-on engineering missions, players learn how to analyze telemetry, make rapid decisions under pressure, and understand the direct environmental consequences of their choices.
  4. Demonstrating Practical Applications of Open Data: Dremo Mars proves how official space agency datasets (from NASA, CSA, and international partners) can be democratized and creatively repurposed into interactive educational tools that make learning both accessible and engaging for kids worldwide.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software that uses to develop the project?

To develop "Dremo Mars," we utilized a robust suite of game development software, coding languages, and AI-assisted workflows:

  1. Game Development Software & Engine:
    • Roblox Studio: Used as the primary 3D game engine and design environment for building the virtual Martian terrain, constructing the 8 interconnected bases, and setting up lighting, physics, and interactive world elements.
    • Luau: Utilized for all in-game scripting, including mission logic, player interactions, mini-games, dynamic environmental triggers, and the "Commander Mode" crisis simulation mechanics.
    • Claude (AI Assistant): Assisted with structuring coding architecture, developing complex game scripts, debugging, and testing features within Roblox Studio.
    • Personal Computer / Workstation: Used for development, 3D modeling, code authoring, and testing performance.
    • UI/UX Design Tools: Utilized for creating user interfaces, child-friendly HUD elements, telemetry dashboards, and the multi-camera view system.

What factors did our team consider?

During the development of "Dremo Mars," our team carefully considered several key factors to ensure the project was scientifically grounded, engaging, and educational:

  1. Scientific Authenticity & Data Translation: We evaluated how to translate open datasets and parameters from public space agencies (such as solar weather data from DONKI, radiation telemetry from RadLab, and topographical mapping concepts) into intuitive, age-appropriate 3D gameplay mechanics for educational purposes.
  2. Target Audience & Child-Friendly Engagement: We prioritized designing an immersive learning experience specifically for younger learners (such as junior high students). This led us to replace traditional quizzes and pop-ups with a gamified "Commander Mode" and interactive engineering tasks, ensuring learning happens naturally through cause-and-effect gameplay.
  3. Holistic Systems & Closed-Loop Sustainability Concepts: We explored the theoretical challenges of how Martian habitats might operate using minimal external resources. This inspired our 8 interdependent base modules and conceptual features like the "Meat from Air" Bio-Dome (inspired by public challenges like the NASA Deep Space Food Challenge and sustainable food tech concepts), introducing players to closed-loop life support and future food security ideas.
  4. Technical Feasibility & Performance in Roblox: We balanced interactive gameplay features—such as real-time environmental event simulations, telemetry dashboards, multi-camera views, and dynamic UI elements—with optimized Luau scripting and Roblox Studio architecture to ensure smooth performance and a stable user experience.
  5. Scientific Accuracy of Environmental Atmosphere: We carefully integrated real Martian atmospheric science into the game's visuals and lighting. Rather than a standard skybox, the game accurately simulates a rusty orange daytime sky caused by iron-oxide dust, transitioning to a blue sunset during twilight hours, reinforcing real planetary science concepts through immersive visuals.
